concepts.name: G77: Origins and Founding Context
key_dimensions: Founded in 1964 under UNCTAD, not the UN General Assembly directly — a common confusion point
Significance of the 'Joint Declaration of the Seventy-Seven Developing Countries' at UNCTAD I in Geneva
Historical link to the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) and how G77 differs in focus (economic vs. political)
Why the name 'G77' was retained despite membership expansion beyond 77 nations

concepts.name: G77 Membership: Composition and Expansion
key_dimensions: Current membership (~134 countries) vs. founding membership (77) — the 'name vs. reality' trap
China's unique status: member of G77 but NOT the G20 as a 'developing country' — overlap confusion
Which major economies are NOT members (e.g., BRICS members like Russia are not in G77)
India's membership and its dual role as both G77 and G20 member — strategic implications

concepts.name: G77's Institutional Structure and Secretariat
key_dimensions: G77 has NO permanent secretariat — a high-yield trap question
Chairmanship rotates among regional groups (Africa, Asia-Pacific, Latin America & Caribbean)
The role of the 'Chapter system': G77 chapters at UN bodies like UNEP, UNESCO, FAO, UNIDO
How G77 coordinates positions before major UN conferences — consensus-based diplomacy

concepts.name: G77 vs. NAM: Overlaps and Distinctions
key_dimensions: G77 is exclusively economic/developmental in mandate; NAM is political/strategic
Many countries are members of both, but membership criteria differ
G77+China vs. NAM: how China participates differently in each
UPSC trap: Both were products of 1960s decolonization but are structurally and functionally distinct

concepts.name: G77's Relationship with UNCTAD
key_dimensions: G77 was born out of UNCTAD I (1964) — UNCTAD is the primary operational platform for G77 advocacy
G77 uses UNCTAD to push for New International Economic Order (NIEO) principles
UNCTAD vs. WTO: G77's preference for UNCTAD as a more development-friendly forum
Annual UNCTAD meetings and G77's bloc negotiating strategy

concepts.name: New International Economic Order (NIEO) and G77
key_dimensions: NIEO Declaration of 1974: G77's landmark push for restructuring global trade and finance
Key demands: commodity price stabilization, technology transfer, debt relief, reform of IMF/World Bank
Why NIEO failed: opposition from developed nations, collapse of commodity prices in 1980s
Legacy of NIEO in current G77 demands at climate finance and WTO negotiations

concepts.name: G77+China Configuration
key_dimensions: 'G77+China' is the operational name used in UN negotiations — China is an associate, not a full member
Why China aligns with G77 despite being world's second-largest economy — strategic positioning
Tensions within G77+China: smaller developing nations vs. China's economic dominance
India-China dynamics within G77+China at climate (UNFCCC) and trade negotiations

concepts.name: G77 and Climate Change Negotiations (UNFCCC)
key_dimensions: G77+China is the largest negotiating bloc at COP meetings — 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) advocacy
Internal fractures: AOSIS (small island states) vs. BASIC (Brazil, South Africa, India, China) within G77
G77's demand for Loss and Damage funding — COP27 breakthrough and G77's role
Distinction between G77's climate demands and G20's climate commitments — where India sits

concepts.name: G77 and UN General Assembly Voting Dynamics
key_dimensions: G77 as a majority bloc in UNGA — can pass resolutions given 'one nation, one vote' principle
Contrast with UN Security Council where P5 veto neutralizes G77 majority
G77's use of UNGA for pushing Sustainable Development agenda and South-South cooperation resolutions
UPSC angle: Why UNGA resolutions pushed by G77 are 'non-binding' yet politically significant

concepts.name: South-South Cooperation and G77
key_dimensions: G77 as the primary institutional champion of South-South Cooperation (SSC) at the UN
Buenos Aires Plan of Action (1978) — foundational document for SSC emerging from G77 context
Distinction between South-South Cooperation and North-South aid — conditionality vs. solidarity
India's role in SSC: ITEC, IAFS, and alignment with G77 principles

concepts.name: G77 Annual Summit and Chairmanship
key_dimensions: Annual Ministerial Meeting held in New York during UNGA session — significance of timing
G77 Summit of Heads of State — rare but high-profile (e.g., Havana 2000, Santa Cruz 2014)
Chairmanship by regional rotation: Africa, Asia-Pacific, GRULAC (Latin America & Caribbean), and others
2023 Chairmanship held by Cuba — implications for agenda-setting

concepts.name: G77 and Global Financial Architecture Reform
key_dimensions: G77's consistent demand for reform of IMF voting rights and World Bank governance
Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) allocation — G77's push for equitable distribution post-COVID
Debt relief and sovereign debt restructuring: G77's position at G20 and UN platforms
Comparison with G20's 'Common Framework' for debt — why G77 finds it inadequate

concepts.name: G77 and Technology Transfer
key_dimensions: Technology transfer has been a G77 demand since NIEO (1974) — continuity of the issue
TRIPS Agreement and G77's position: flexibilities for developing countries vs. IP protection
G77's push within WIPO for a 'Development Agenda' — adopted 2007
COVID-19 vaccine waiver debate at WTO: G77 solidarity vs. developed country resistance

concepts.name: G77 and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
key_dimensions: G77 played a key role in shaping the SDG framework (2015) — more inclusive than MDGs
G77's insistence on 'Means of Implementation' (finance, technology, capacity building) as SDG 17
Financing for Development (FfD): Addis Ababa Action Agenda and G77's dissatisfaction
UPSC trap: MDGs were top-down (UN-led); SDGs were bottom-up with strong G77 input

concepts.name: G77 Internal Heterogeneity and Fault Lines
key_dimensions: Wide income disparity within G77: oil-rich Gulf states vs. LDCs — common position challenge
OPEC members within G77 vs. oil-importing developing nations on energy pricing
Small Island Developing States (SIDS) vs. large emerging economies on climate ambition
UPSC angle: How G77 maintains consensus despite internal contradictions — 'unity of diversity' trap

concepts.name: G77 vs. G20: Complementarity and Contradiction
key_dimensions: G20 includes major G77 members (India, China, Brazil, South Africa) but represents ~85% of global GDP
G77 represents 'all' developing countries; G20 is selective — legitimacy vs. effectiveness debate
Issues where G77 and G20 align: SDG financing, climate finance; Issues where they diverge: debt relief speed
India's balancing act: championing G77 causes while being a G20 member — 'Voice of the Global South'

concepts.name: India's Strategic Role within G77
key_dimensions: India as a founding member and consistent advocate of G77 principles
India's 'Voice of Global South' initiative (2023) — aligning with G77 agenda during G20 presidency
India's push for African Union's inclusion in G20 — seen as extension of G77 solidarity
Tension: India's growing economy and interests sometimes diverge from LDC-dominated G77 positions

concepts.name: G77 and WTO Negotiations
key_dimensions: G77 members form overlapping coalitions at WTO: G33, G90, African Group, ACP — not one monolithic bloc
Doha Development Round and G77's demand for agricultural subsidy cuts by developed nations
Special and Differential Treatment (S&DT) — G77's core WTO demand for developing country flexibilities
UPSC trap: G77 as such does not negotiate at WTO; country coalitions do — institutional distinction

concepts.name: G77 Declarations and Key Documents
key_dimensions: 1964 Joint Declaration (Geneva) — founding document
1974 NIEO Declaration and Programme of Action — most cited G77 achievement at UNGA
2000 Havana Programme of Action — South-South Cooperation framework
Santa Cruz Declaration (2014) — on 'For a New World Order for Living Well' — Bolivia summit

concepts.name: G77 and Multilateralism: Relevance in a Fragmented World
key_dimensions: G77's role in defending UN-centric multilateralism against G7/G20 dominated forums
Rise of minilateralism (Quad, AUKUS, I2U2) and its challenge to G77's universal approach
G77's position on UN Security Council reform — permanent seats for developing nations
Post-COVID and post-Ukraine war: G77's push for 'development-first' global agenda vs. geopolitical priorities
